parent_preregistration.inherited: bulk and brane potentials, portal, basis, cubic couplings, mass matching, constants, parameter grid and validity flags are identical to the parent and are not restated or changed here

author_direction: Kirk LaSalle approved taking selected Candidate B further on 2026-10-16 with two tests: a width-matched CMS-HIG-24-002 heavy-scalar comparison and a correlated Higgs-rate likelihood.
registration_scope: Local prospective numerical preregistration, frozen by SHA-256 before the ATLAS global signal-strength scan values (AuxFig1*.yaml) and before any CMS-HIG-24-002 limit values, observed or expected, were read into this workspace. It is not an external registry entry.
prior_knowledge_disclosure: The ATLAS headline global signal strength mu = 1.05 +/- 0.06 (paper abstract) was known. The approximate location of the likelihood crossings is therefore predictable; test A is not blind to its approximate outcome. Its value is a fixed rule applied to the published profile likelihood.
The first Candidate B test outcome was known: compatible_with_limit with kappa_lo = 0.97591 from the ATLAS (kappa_V, kappa_F) observed 95% contour.

For CMS-HIG-24-002 only file names, table descriptions, qualifiers and independent-variable (mass and width) grids were inspected. No limit value was read. General awareness of typical LHC ZZ-resonance limit magnitudes exists.

A model-only survey at kappa = 0.976 and 0.90 on the parent grid found heavy-state total widths <= 31 GeV where the width table is tabulated and <= 55 GeV above it. This fixed the width hypotheses below; no data value was used.
The HXSWG theory tables were retrieved and extracted before this freeze. They are model inputs, not outcome data.

model_extension.higgs_rates: every production x decay rate of the 125 GeV state is kappa^2 times its SM value (mu = kappa^2 <= 1), with SM kinematics and no decays to undetected or new states
model_extension.heavy_production: sigma_p,a = u_a^2 sigma_p^SM-like(M_a) for p in {ggF, VBF}, u_a = U[0,a]; gluon fusion proceeds only through the SM quark loops because the model adds no coloured states
model_extension.heavy_width: Gamma_a = u_a^2 Gamma_SM_total(M_a) + Gamma_a->scalar pairs, the latter from the parent tree-level cubic tensor
model_extension.states: every eigenstate a >= 1 (all states except the matched 125 GeV state)

theory_inputs.cross_sections: HXSWG YR4 BSM 13 TeV page r30: ggF quark-loop induced NNLO+NNLL (sigma column, without the separate 1+delta_EW factor) and VBF approximate NNLO; tabulated 10-3000 GeV
theory_inputs.widths: HXSWG YR3 2013-update page r16: SM BR(ZZ) and total width, tabulated 80-1000 GeV
theory_inputs.interpolation: log sigma linear in M; BR_ZZ linear in M; log Gamma_SM_total linear in M
theory_inputs.extrapolation_above_1000_GeV: Gamma_SM_total(M) = k_tot Gamma_tree(M) and Gamma_SM_ZZ(M) = k_ZZ Gamma_tree_ZZ(M), with Gamma_tree the parent on-shell WW + ZZ + t tbar formula and k fixed by continuity at M = 1000 GeV. States using this are labelled extrapolated and reported separately from the primary result.
theory_inputs.theory_low_variant: sigma x (1 - sqrt(scale_down^2 + (PDF+alpha_s)^2)) x min(1, 1 + delta_EW where provided for ggF)

test_a_higgs_rate_likelihood.data_product: ATLAS Nature 607 (2022) 52, HEPData ins2104706 v1 original submission (pinned zip), AuxFig1.yaml 'Aux Figure 8 (Total)': observed -2 ln Lambda(mu) for the global signal strength, all systematic uncertainties included, sqrt(s) = 13 TeV
test_a_higgs_rate_likelihood.validity: the restricted model predicts exactly the global-mu hypothesis (universal rate scaling, SM kinematics), so the published one-parameter profile likelihood applies with mu = kappa^2
test_a_higgs_rate_likelihood.interpolation: L(mu) = -2 ln Lambda(mu) linear between scan points; no extrapolation beyond the scan
test_a_higgs_rate_likelihood.reference: mu_hat = scan point with minimum L; reference point mu_ref = min(mu_hat, 1)
test_a_higgs_rate_likelihood.family_test: q_family = L(1) - L(mu_hat) if mu_hat > 1, else 0; asymptotic test of H0: mu <= 1 with the 1/2 chi2_0 + 1/2 chi2_1 null distribution
test_a_higgs_rate_likelihood.primary_statistic: q(mu) = L(mu) - L(mu_ref) for mu <= mu_ref
test_a_higgs_rate_likelihood.primary_limit: mu_lo = the largest mu < mu_ref with q(mu) = 2.706 (first crossing below mu_ref); kappa_lo = sqrt(mu_lo); mu4_max(R, m5, Lambda) solves kappa(mu4) = kappa_lo on the parent grid. Referencing the physical boundary is never less conservative than the unbounded one-sided limit.
sensitivity: unbounded one-sided: crossing of L(mu) - L(mu_hat) = 2.706 below mu_hat
two-sided 95%: crossing of L(mu) - L(mu_hat) = 3.841 below mu_hat
primary rule applied to AuxFig1_2 (background theory fixed), AuxFig1_3 (signal and background theory fixed) and AuxFig1_4 (statistical only); these understate uncertainty and are never the result
M_H = 125.2 GeV for the mu4_max translation

outcome_rules.incompatible: q_family > 2.706: the whole restricted family (mu <= 1) is disfavoured at asymptotic 95% CL by the published likelihood
outcome_rules.compatible_with_limit: q_family <= 2.706 and mu_lo lies inside the scan: report mu_lo, kappa_lo and mu4_max per valid grid point
outcome_rules.not_determinable: q_family <= 2.706 but the crossing lies below the first scan point: report only that mu_lo is below that point; do not extrapolate
outcome_rules.ambiguous_data: wrong file, qualifier or description, non-finite values, or fewer than two scan points below mu_ref: stop and report

test_b_cms_direct_resonance.data_product: CMS-HIG-24-002, HEPData ins3161000 v1 original submission (pinned zip): 95% CL upper limits on sigma(pp -> X) x BR(X -> ZZ) in pb at 13 TeV, 138 fb^-1, separately for ggF and VBF production
test_b_cms_direct_resonance.tables: Limits_{NWA,W1,W10,W100}_{ggH,VBFH}.yaml; 'Observed' for the result and 'Expected median' for sensitivity. The 2D mass-width scans and the VBF-fraction-profiled table are not used.
test_b_cms_direct_resonance.limit_rule: for a state (M, Gamma) take the bracketing width hypotheses w_lo <= Gamma <= w_hi (a single hypothesis on an exact match) and, in each of those tables, the bracketing table masses m_lo <= M <= m_hi (a single mass on an exact match). The primary limit is the maximum observed limit over these at most four points (conservative envelope).
test_b_cms_direct_resonance.coverage: a state is covered if 130 <= M <= 3000 GeV and Gamma <= 100 GeV in both production tables; uncovered states are listed, not compared
test_b_cms_direct_resonance.state_ratio: r_a = max(sigma_ggF,a BR_ZZ,a / L_ggF(M_a, Gamma_a), sigma_VBF,a BR_ZZ,a / L_VBF(M_a, Gamma_a)); each production mode is compared alone, ignoring the other component
test_b_cms_direct_resonance.theory_categories: tabulated: M_a <= 1000 GeV (all theory inputs tabulated); extrapolated: 1000 < M_a <= 3000 GeV. The primary result uses tabulated states only; the result including extrapolated states is reported separately.
test_b_cms_direct_resonance.mu4_scan: for each valid parent grid point, mu4_k = k mu4(kappa = 0.90) / 100 for k = 1..100, with R(mu4) = max over covered states of r_a. Report every excluded scan point. mu4_excl_min is refined by 30 bisection steps between the last non-excluded point (or 0) and the first excluded point.
test_b_cms_direct_resonance.comparison_with_rate_bounds: per grid point, state whether mu4_excl_min is below mu4_max from the first test (contour) and from test A (likelihood)
sensitivity: expected median limits instead of observed
limit linearly interpolated in mass (log limit) instead of the mass envelope, keeping the width envelope
test_b_cms_direct_resonance.secondary_heuristic_tower_clusters: for W in {10, 100} GeV and each covered state j, S_p,j = sum over states a with |M_a - M_j| <= W/2 and Gamma_a <= W of sigma_p,a BR_ZZ,a, compared with the W-table limit at M_j under the mass envelope. Report the smallest scanned mu4 at which any ratio exceeds 1. Labelled heuristic: a cluster of discrete narrow states is treated as one resonance of width W and interference is neglected.

outcome_rules_per_grid_point.exclusion_above_rate_bounds: excluded scan points exist but mu4_excl_min >= the smaller Higgs-rate mu4_max
outcome_rules_per_grid_point.exclusion_within_rate_allowed_region: mu4_excl_min < the smaller Higgs-rate mu4_max: the direct search is the stronger constraint at that point
outcome_rules_per_grid_point.not_covered: no covered state at any scanned mu4

test_b_cms_direct_resonance.overall_scope: mu4 = 0 is the SM limit and produces no heavy-state signal, so this test can only bound mu4; it cannot exclude the restricted family

combined_statement: per grid point the reported bound is min(mu4_max from the Higgs-rate tests, mu4_excl_min from CMS). It is the intersection of separate 95% CL-type constraints, not a joint statistical combination.
caveats: interference with the gg -> ZZ continuum, the off-shell 125 GeV tail and among nearby tower states is neglected
comparing each production mode alone ignores the other component; this is standard practice but not a rigorous bound
signal acceptance and shapes are assumed to match the CMS SM-like scalar hypothesis
heavy-state scalar widths are tree level; SM-like widths above 1 TeV are extrapolated
asymptotic likelihood statistics; no toy calibration
forbidden: editing this file, the theory-input table or the parent preregistration after the freeze
choosing among envelope, interpolation, width or variant rules after reading limit or likelihood values
adding width hypotheses, tables or grid points after reading values
combining CMS and ATLAS into a joint likelihood or quoting a joint p-value
treating compatibility, or a surviving parameter range, as confirmation of Candidate B
